title: Eval Integration Toolbelt — practical notes and quick scripts
content:
Purpose:
Quick, practical collection of patterns and tiny helper scripts for model onboarding evals. This is intended to be a lightweight companion to the formal eval-harness design docs — a place for tried tricks, gotchas, and runnable snippets that people can copy into PRs.

Scope / audience:
- Engineers onboarding models (applied-ml, platform) who need fast iteration loops.
- SRE/devs who wire CI for eval regressions.
- Solutions/SEs preparing prompt sets for customers.

High-level constraints we care about:
- Reproducibility: single-command local smoke that mirrors CI.
- Low-friction: tiny python CLIs or bash wrappers (no heavy deps for simple checks).
- Coverage: must exercise generation config, temperature, stop tokens, and model variants (quantized/float).
- Speed: make fast paths for small prompt sets (~50 queries) and separate heavy nightly suites.

Quick architecture sketch (how pieces fit):
- prompt_sets/ (yaml or jsonl fixtures) -> loader (streaming or batch) -> runner (sync/async) -> scoring module -> report generator -> CI gate.
- Runner should be thin: translate harness request -> model client (hosted/dedicated/private) -> capture raw tokens, latency, reasons (timeouts, truncated).

Useful small scripts (place under evals/tools/):
1) smoke_run.py (CLI)
- usage: python smoke_run.py --model rwd-v1 --prompts ./prompt_sets/sanity.jsonl --out tmp/sanity_run.json
- does: loads first N prompts (default 20), runs with deterministic seed, writes raw responses and token cost summary.
- skeleton:
  from argparse import ArgumentParser
  import json, random
  parser = ArgumentParser()
  # parse args, set fixed seed random.seed(42)
  # load up to N prompts, call runner.run_sync(), dump results

2) loader_fastpath.py
- goal: single-file loader that supports three modes: jsonl (one sample per line), csv (col:prompt,ref), and small sqlite bundle for >100k samples.
- pattern: yield dicts so runner can stream and not materialize dataset. Example interface: for sample in loader(path, mode): yield {"id":..., "prompt":..., "meta":{}}

3) score_utils.py
- functions: normalize_text(s), exact_match(pred, gold), span_f1(pred, gold), normalized_levenshtein(pred, gold), embed_similarity(pred, gold, model='text-embedding-ada-002').
- tie into thresholds: report passes if metric >= threshold. Keep thresholds in a tiny config YAML per eval suite.

Loader patterns and recommendations:
- Streaming loader (generator) for large datasets — avoids memory blowups.
- Shardable ID scheme: <suite>-YYYYMMDD-shard-0001 so CI can parallelize by shard.
- Lightweight fixtures (small): keep a curated set of 30-100 prompts hitting edge cases: long context, stop-token boundaries, unusual tokens (unicode), multi-turn scaffolding.
- Golden-baselines: store golden responses as tokenized canonical strings (normalize whitespace + punctuation) to avoid incidental diffs.

Scoring function design decisions (notes):
- Prefer tolerant metrics for generation onboarding: normalized-levenshtein or sentence-embed sim for free-form answers; exact-match for structured outputs.
- Use task-specific metric where possible (e.g., SQL canonicalization then exact-match; extracted entities using span-F1).
- Combine metrics: primary (task metric) + secondary (perplexity delta / safety checks).
- Keep scoring functions pure and isolated (no external service calls). If embed-sim required, cache embeddings in repo or CI artifact to avoid flakiness.

Regression reporting and thresholds:
- Two-tier gating: immediate PR smoke (fast suite, <5m) + nightly full-suite (heavy).
- PR gate: fail on any regression > X% absolute drop in primary metric OR new safety hits. Keep X small (1–3% depending on task).
- Baseline storage: /evals/baselines/<model>-<suite>-baseline.json with aggregated metrics and per-sample scores.
- Diff tool: small script that reads new run json and baseline, outputs human-friendly markdown with: summary, top 10 worsened samples (show prompt, gold, baseline pred, new pred), and histogram of delta by decile.
- Example command: python evals/tools/report_diff.py --baseline baselines/rwd-v1-q1-sanity.json --run tmp/latest.json --out tmp/report.md

CI wiring (practical how-to):
- Use lightweight GitHub Actions for PR smoke:
  - job uses smallest GPU (or mock clients) and runs smoke_run.py on curated fixture.
  - output artifacts: raw run json + condensed markdown report.
  - post summary comment using GH Action that only flags failure when primary metric regression exceeds threshold.
- Nightly: separate workflow that runs on schedule, can use larger dedicated pools. Save artifacts to S3 or GHA artifacts, and update baseline if run is approved.
- Protect baseline updates: only run after manual review or when model is promoted via release pipeline.

Local dev loop tips:
- Provide Dockerfile that installs only test deps and a tiny config to point at mock client (record/replay mode).
- Provide run_local.sh: builds a small container, runs smoke suite, opens report via 'python -m http.server' against tmp/report.html for quick eyeballing.
- Keep --max-requests and --parallel flags so devs can throttle costs.

Reproducibility decisions:
- Fix RNG seeds for sampling components where possible; but we must also track 'sampling_mode' in run metadata.
- Save full request/response traces including generation config, seed, timestamp, model variant ID.
- Tokenization: record tokenizer name and tokenized ids for baseline and run to help debug tokenization-related diffs.

Common gotchas and troubleshooting notes:
- ‘‘Flaky’’ failures often caused by embedding-based metrics using live embed service — cache embeddings and version them.
- Tokenization drift when switching toolkit versions (huggingface/tokenizers), pin tokenizer libs in CI.
- Different model variants (quantized/float, different compilation kernels) may change whitespace or punctuation heuristics — prefer normalized scoring.
- Large-case diffs from newer models that add polite framing — consider optional post-processors to strip polite prefixes for comparison.

Mini-spec: minimal PR-gating pipeline (example)
1) PR opens -> run: evals/pr-smoke workflow
2) smoke workflow pulls curated fixture, runs smoke_run.py against candidate model (or shadow)
3) smoke_run produces tmp/run.json -> run report_diff.py against baselines/* -> if primary_metric_delta < -THRESH: post comment PASS/FAIL + attach report
4) On FAIL: label PR with eval-regression; link to sample cases for debugging.

Example small JSON run artifact (fields to include):
- run_id, model_id, variant_tag, seed, run_time_s, metrics:{primary:0.873, secondary:...}, per_sample:[{id, prompt, gold, pred, score, latency_ms, token_count}]

Checklist before adding a new eval suite:
- [ ] curated fixture: 30–100 focused prompts (jsonl)
- [ ] scoring function implemented + unit tests (pytest)
- [ ] smoke loader + small-run script in evals/tools/
- [ ] baseline generated and uploaded to baselines/ with metadata
- [ ] CI smoke workflow added to .github/workflows/ with artifact upload
- [ ] doc: short README in suite folder explaining purpose and thresholds

Open questions (to resolve in follow-ups):
- When to automatically rebaseline? Manual gating seems safer but slows iteration. Propose: auto-update baseline only for non-production model tags (experimental/*) after N consecutive green nightly runs.
- How best to standardize embedding similarity thresholds across diverse tasks? Need a calibration suite.

TODO (next quick patches):
- [ ] Add record/replay helper for hosted API to reproduce transient latency spikes (Sasha).
- [ ] Small utility to canonicalize SQL outputs before exact-match (Priya).
- [ ] Short cookbook snippet for writing a custom scoring plugin (Michael).

Notes to self:
- Keep this doc intentionally informal; move stable patterns into eval-harness repo docs.
- When in doubt, prefer reproducibility over convenience (store seeds, tokens, config).

If you copy any snippet from here into a PR: make it self-contained (one-file), and add a short test that runs in <60s.

End of notes.
